title: Identification of local nonlinear shear-wave dynamics using Volterra kernels: application to prostate cancer detection.
source: PubMed · IEEE transactions on medical imaging
desc: [IEEE transactions on medical imaging] Cancer remains a major health concern worldwide. Shear-wave elastography (SWE) holds promise for cancer detection by quantifying linear elastic changes in tissue through shear-wave (SW) velocity estimation. However, shear viscosity and nonlinearity are often over-looked, despite their potential as additional biomarkers. This study evaluates the visco-hyperelastic properties of soft tissue, including linear shear modulus, shear viscosity, and shear nonlinearity. We propose using Volterra kernels to characterize local nonlinear SW dynamics, with kernel identification based on SW particle velocity measurements at adjacent locations. The method was validated using in-silico simulations and in-vitro gelatin phantoms. To evaluate its clinical relevance, we applied the method for prostate cancer (PCa) detection. To our knowledge, this is the first in-vivo assessment of voxel-based visco-hyperelastic properties of the prostate. In 90 patients, our results indicated that the linear kernel correlated with the linear shear modulus, while the quadratic kernel reflected both viscosity and nonlinearity. A convolutional neural network trained on these parameters with registered histopathology as ground truth achieved area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) values of 0.60 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.57, 0.62) and 0.66 (95% CI: 0.64, 0.68) for PCa detection, respectively-both significantly outperforming the linear shear modulus (AUC of 0.54; 95% CI, 0.52 to 0.56). Our findings suggest that Volterra kernels reflect information related to the visco-hyperelastic properties of prostate tissue, highlighting the potential of viscosity and nonlinearity as additional biomarkers for PCa detection.

title: Patient attitudes toward artificial intelligence-driven dermatology.
source: PubMed · The Journal of investigative dermatology
desc: [The Journal of investigative dermatology] Artificial intelligence (AI) systems are increasingly being developed for dermatology, but the conditions under which patients trust these tools remain poorly characterized. This Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses-guided systematic narrative review synthesizes peer-reviewed empirical studies, published from January 1, 2015 through July 7, 2026, that directly assessed patient or public attitudes toward AI in dermatologic diagnosis, skin-cancer screening, image sharing, teledermatology image-quality support, and related patient-facing workflows. Eligible evidence included qualitative interviews and focus groups, surveys, preference/conjoint or vignette experiments, and early clinical deployments. Twenty studies met the inclusion criteria using the review framework. Across study designs, patients expressed conditional support for dermatology AI but consistently favored dermatologist-supervised AI over autonomous AI, especially for high-stakes diagnostic decisions. Trust was strengthened by visible clinician accountability, clear explanations of AI outputs and uncertainty, privacy safeguards, transparent data use, and evidence that performance is reliable across skin tone and diagnosis. Trust declined when AI was framed as replacing clinicians, when image governance was unclear, or when unequal performance was perceived. These findings support a model of augmented intelligence: dermatology AI should serve the clinical relationship; be subject to human oversight; and be evaluated and reported stratified by skin tone, diagnosis, and care context.

title: Prospective AI-Assisted Screening of Biliary Tract Cancer Using Non-Contrast CT
desc: [Newly registered clinical trial, no results yet; sponsor: Beijing Tsinghua Chang Gung Hospital; conditions: Biliary Tract Cancer (BTC); type: INTERVENTIONAL; phase: NA; enrollment: 10000; status: NOT_YET_RECRUITING] Biliary tract cancer is a group of malignant tumors involving the intrahepatic bile ducts, extrahepatic bile ducts, and gallbladder. Early detection can be challenging because non-contrast computed tomography (NCCT), which is commonly performed in routine clinical practice, may provide limited information for identifying biliary tract cancer. This prospective study aims to clinically validate an artificial intelligence (AI) system for screening and detecting biliary tract cancer on NCCT images. The AI system will independently analyze eligible NCCT examinations and generate a patient-level risk score for biliary tract cancer. The study will evaluate the diagnostic performance of the AI system against a predefined clinical reference standard. The primary objective is to assess the ability of the AI system to distinguish patients with biliary tract cancer from those without biliary tract cancer using NCCT. Secondary objectives include evaluating sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, and negative predictive value. The study is designed to evaluate the clinical performance and potential screening value of AI-assisted analysis of NCCT. Routine clinical care and clinical decision-making will not be replaced by the AI system.

title: MemSteer: Turning User Histories into Supervision for Agent Memory Optimization
desc: An effective agent memory system should adapt to a user's history and task requirements. Human-annotated supervision can guide this adaptation by providing feedback for evaluating and improving memory designs. Yet suitable labels are rarely available for new user histories, and manually constructing QA pairs and supporting evidence is costly. We introduce MemSteer, which turns unlabeled user histories into question-answer (QA) supervision with supporting evidence for memory-design optimization. MemSteer constructs an evidence-grounded answer plan that specifies how facts across related records jointly support a reference answer. The plan guides question generation, while source-grounded auditing and blind answer recovery check the resulting annotations. To study the utility of this supervision, we develop MemSteer-Opt, which combines QA-based design evaluation with evidence-guided failure diagnosis to revise memory store, retrieval, and context construction without updating model parameters. Experiments on ATM-Bench and RHELM show that this supervision is competitive with official-QA-guided optimization. Relative to Base-BM25, MemSteer-Opt improves ATM-Bench Question Score by 13.4 points and RHELM accuracy by 4.1 and 6.6 points without and with external data, respectively. The supervision also benefits two existing optimizers on ATM-Bench, while new-user experiments demonstrate continued design optimization using supervision generated from the target histories.

title: Identifying interstitial lung disease with large language models on clinical notes and claims
desc: Interstitial lung disease (ILD) is a potentially fatal toxicity of immune checkpoint inhibitors and antibody-drug conjugates. Drug-safety studies in healthcare databases identify ILD with claims-based algorithms that trade positive predictive value (PPV) against sensitivity. We assessed whether large language models (LLMs) improve on these algorithms, with and without electronic health record (EHR) notes, and whether these gains translate into measurable epidemiological benefits. In 309 oncology patients with ILD diagnosis codes at Mass General Brigham, adjudicated by two pulmonologists, we compared 12 open-access LLMs with 20 published claims-based algorithms. LLMs received claims, EHR notes, or both, without task-specific training. Measures were PPV and yield (proportion classified positive). We projected the attenuation of a drug-induced ILD odds ratio under non-differential outcome misclassification. LLMs extended the PPV-yield frontier of the published algorithms with all three inputs. Across the 36 model--input evaluations, LLM PPV exceeded that of the best algorithm without specialist-coding requirements (Algorithm 4) by 14.3 percentage points on average. With claims alone, Qwen3-8B achieved 89.8% PPV (95% CI 78.2-95.6) at 15.9% yield, versus 86.7% at 4.9% for the highest-PPV algorithm. With notes alone, Qwen3-32B achieved 78.9% PPV at 49.2% yield, versus 64.6% at 51.1% for Algorithm~4. With combined claims and notes, Qwen3-14B achieved 100.0% PPV at 24.3% yield. Under a simulated drug-safety scenario with a true odds ratio of 3.0, the projected observed odds ratio was 2.67 with combined inputs versus 1.07 with Algorithm 4, corresponding to a 46-fold difference in the estimated sample size required for 80% power (591 versus 27,200 patients). Zero-shot LLMs offer a higher-PPV alternative to rule-based claims phenotyping for ILD, on all three input types. Because the claims-only configuration uses the same claims data as existing algorithms, it could be deployed in administrative databases without linked notes, and may recover drug-safety signal otherwise lost to outcome misclassification.

title: Conversational Interaction for LLM-Based Clinical Text-to-SQL: A User Study with Healthcare Professionals
desc: Conversational text-to-SQL interfaces could give healthcare professionals natural-language access to electronic health record (EHR) data, but evidence for their real-world usability remains limited: prior evaluations have relied largely on curated benchmarks with fully specified questions or on simulated users. We report a user study in which 14 physicians who regularly work with EHR data used both a single-turn and a conversational multi-turn text-to-SQL interface over the MIMIC-IV database in a within-subjects design; dialogue analyses additionally drew on interaction logs from 21 healthcare professionals across the main study and two pilot studies. The conversational interface was consistently favored: mean System Usability Scale scores rose from 68.2, near the industry average, to 85.9 (p<0.001), with significant advantages across technology-acceptance constructs including performance expectancy, effort expectancy, self-efficacy, and behavioral intention. In post-study forced-choice comparisons, 93% of participants reported greater overall satisfaction with the conversational interface, 86% preferred it for real-world adoption, and 71% trusted its results more; no participant preferred or trusted the single-turn interface more. Turn-level analysis of 425 logged user turns showed that freely composed queries triggered clarification requests in 24.8% of cases versus 1.8% for predefined, fully specified questions, and 64.3% of clarification episodes stemmed from EHR- or clinical-domain knowledge. Conversational interaction is a practical prerequisite, rather than a convenience, for natural-language EHR access. The frequent need for clarification in realistic clinical queries further underscores the importance of conversational interfaces, while benchmark-style evaluation can substantially underrepresent the ambiguity of real clinical use.

title: ToxINsight: An Integrated Web Platform for Sequence, Structure, and Ligand Binding Analysis of Snake Venom Toxins
desc: Around 5.4 million people worldwide are bitten by snakes each year, with 1.8 to 2.7 million cases of envenomation, of which 81,410 to 137,880 people die from snake envenomation worldwide each year. It is categorized as a high-priority Category A Neglected Tropical Disease (NTD) by the World Health Organization (WHO). A molecular level understanding of snake venom toxins and their mechanisms of action is crucial for development of efficient therapeutics tackling snake envenomation. Snake venoms are complex mixtures of bioactive peptides and proteins that have also served as templates for drug discovery. Resources dedicated to snake venom toxins sequence, structure, functions, geographical distributions and molecular-level analysis remain fragmented across general-purpose repositories. Here we present ToxINsight, an integrated, freely accessible database and web-based analysis platform built exclusively for snake venom toxins. ToxINsight curates 2,078 toxin entries spanning 11 medically and scientifically relevant snake toxin families across 237 venomous snake species from five different snake families, and provides 2,540 three-dimensional structures associated with these entries, which are assembled from the RCSB Protein Data Bank , AlphaFold DB and ESMFold-generated 3D models. ToxINsight offers built-in tools alongside toxin records for comparisons and analysis of toxin sequences and structures and their properties for efficient target selection and prioritization. ToxINsight allow the user to select multiple entries and align them, or select a pair of entries to compare structural and physicochemical properties. ToxINsight provides all reported-ligand annotations for each toxin entry, and bulk export of sequence, structure, and metadata for building sequence and/or structure based machine learning models . ToxINsight also offers a visual ATLAS, which provides geographical information about venomous snake families/species for a more focused understanding of snake venom toxins across different geographical landscapes. By combining sequence, structure, ligand and geographical information along with analysis and comparative tools in a single interface, ToxINsight is designed to support and encourage researchers across the world towards the development of efficient targeted therapeutics against snake venom toxins from diverse families.
